The fire, which occurred on Thursday, was contained by firefighters, police officers and community members, with no life lost.
The Cross River State Police Command, in a statement issued after the fire incident by its spokesperson, ASP Eitokpah Sunday Akata, stated that the Divisional Police Officer of Akim Division mobilised the Federal Fire Service to the scene following a distress report.
“Police patrol teams, operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit, VCRU, personnel of the Federal Fire Service and community members worked together to contain the inferno,” the statement said.
Preliminary accounts suggested that the outbreak might have been caused by an electrical spark associated with a lightning strike during a heavy thunderstorm.
However, the police said the actual cause of the fire had not been established, adding that investigations were ongoing.
Calabar has witnessed several fire outbreaks in recent months, including a fire at Akim Timber Market in March which destroyed shops and goods, an August fire at SPAR shopping mall, and another incident at Ekondo street where property that worth millions of naira were destroyed leaving some retirees homeless.
The Command, in collaboration with the State Fire Service, has commenced an investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the latest incident and assess the extent of the damage.
The Commissioner of Police, Cross River State, CP Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, urged residents and business owners to observe fire safety precautions, particularly during thunderstorms.
